record.paper_title: Finite-density lattice QCD and sign problem: current status and open problems
record.original_question: Can the complex Langevin method be made reliable in the low-temperature, finite-density hadron phase of QCD, where the singular drift problem caused by near-zero fermion determinants presently spoils the method? This includes whether deformations, generalized cooling, contour-based hybrids, or other ideas can remove or control the singularity-driven failures without changing the target theory.

evidence.quote: While various methods were proposed, all of them have pros and cons, and there is no established approach to the finite-density region of the hadron phase of QCD. The search for better methods is ongoing.

Low temperature There is no µ-dependence up to µ < mπ/2, and violent phase fluctuation sets in at µ = mπ/2. It is hard to study this parameter region by using the methods based on the importance sampling. To apply the complex Langevin method, one has to solve the difficulty associated with the singularity.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider lattice QCD with a nonzero quark chemical potential μ. The Euclidean path-integral weight, after integrating out the quarks, takes the form det M(U;μ) e^{-S_g[U]}, where U denotes the SU(3) gauge link variables, S_g is the gauge action, and M is the lattice Dirac operator including the quark mass. For μ ≠ 0 the fermion determinant det M(U;μ) is in general complex, so standard importance sampling is obstructed (the "sign problem").

The complex Langevin (CL) method addresses this by complexifying the gauge degrees of freedom (U ∈ SL(3,ℂ) instead of SU(3)) and evolving them by a stochastic differential equation in fictitious Langevin time, with drift derived from the complexified action S_eff = S_g − log det M. Expectation values are computed as long-time averages along the CL trajectory.

In the low-temperature, finite-density "hadron phase" regime (in particular for μ ≳ m_π/2 where the sign problem becomes severe), the eigenvalues of M accumulate near zero, making the drift term ∂(log det M) singular. This "singular-drift problem" causes the formal justification of CL to break down and produces biased or incorrect expectation values. Auxiliary techniques such as gauge cooling, deformation of the action followed by extrapolation, contour deformations, and hybrid schemes have been proposed but none is established as fully reliable in this regime.

Problem: Determine whether there exists a modification of the complex Langevin method — for instance via a generalized cooling procedure, a deformation-and-extrapolation scheme, a contour-deformation hybrid, or some other systematically controlled prescription — which (i) does not alter the target lattice QCD theory in its physical limit, (ii) provably or demonstrably evades the singular-drift failure caused by near-zero eigenvalues of the Dirac operator, and (iii) yields correct expectation values throughout the low-temperature, finite-density hadron phase of QCD. Equivalently, prove that no such modification exists.
artifact.category_tag: Complex Langevin / lattice QCD sign problem
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (including a 2025 study on CL validity near the deconfining transition) confirms that the complex Langevin method still fails in the low-temperature, finite-density hadron regime due to the singular-drift problem associated with near-zero Dirac eigenvalues. Various mitigations (gauge cooling, deformation technique, etc.) extend the applicable region but none reliably covers the hadron phase. The problem is still open.

status_evidence.title: On the validity of the complex Langevin method near the deconfining phase transition in QCD at finite density
status_evidence.snippet: CL works in a broad region up to μ/T ≈ 4.8 but starts to fail approaching the phase boundary due to the singular drift problem.
status_evidence.claim: As of 2025, the singular-drift problem still causes CL to fail in the relevant low-T finite-density regime.

status_evidence.title: Gauge cooling for the singular-drift problem in the complex Langevin method — finite density QCD
status_evidence.snippet: Gauge cooling proposed to overcome singular-drift in finite density QCD.
status_evidence.claim: Gauge-cooling-based mitigations have been proposed but not established to resolve the hadron-phase regime.

status_evidence.title: Complex Langevin calculations in finite density QCD at large μ/T with the deformation technique
status_evidence.snippet: Deformation technique to overcome singular-drift in large μ/T regime.
status_evidence.claim: Deformation techniques partially extend CL applicability but do not establish reliability in the hadron phase.
